$comment: Every playable traveller, and where their frames come from.
This replaced two hand-written invocations in package.json with a colour count typed into
each. Two characters was tolerable; five characters across seven sheets is not, and the
sitting art is packed two and three to a file, which no command line should have to remember.
A sixth traveller is a row here and nothing else.
walk:  a 4x4 sheet, one character, sixteen frames -- four per facing, in the order
findSprites returns them (down, up, right, left).
sit:   one frame per facing. The new sitting art gives one pose per direction rather than
four, and that is enough: a seated figure has nowhere to walk to. `frames` names which
figures to take from a packed sheet, in reading order, because position-in-row is not
reliable -- see the note on --frames in build-sprite-sheet.js.
colours: per character, never shared. At 26x40 it is hue that tells one person from another,
and quantising three characters together starves all three.

characters.name: Mithra
$walk_comment: Mithra's profile rows arrive the other way round, and only Mithra's do.
findSprites returns this sheet as down, up, LEFT, right -- so the built sheet put the
left-facing art at frames 8-11, which is where WALK_ROW in src/game/player.ts says the
right-facing art lives. Walking east played a figure facing west while it slid east: a
moonwalk, and the one every other character does not do.
Reordered here rather than in the game. The four-row convention is one every other sheet
already keeps, and one character's art should not bend it for the other four. --frames
reorders as well as selects (boxes = wanted.map(...)), so naming all sixteen in the order
the game expects is the whole fix.
Verified by eye at 18x, which is the only way this class of fault is caught: frame 10
faces left and frame 14 faces right in the source, and the pair swap under this list.
